title: Feet That Find the Ground: Reaching Down Until Contact, a Ground Height Learned From Each Landing, and a Hole Told From a Step

questions.question: How does a foot with no camera for the ground deal with a step down?
options: It lands where expected and keeps reaching down until the contact sense says it is down
It lowers the whole body until all four feet report contact
It ends the swing higher, so that it always lands with a margin
It uses the height the last foot found and steps to that
questions.explanation: The foot is taken to where the ground was expected and then reaches down at a bounded rate until the contact sense of 34-07 says it is down.

questions.question: A step down of 5 cm took an extension of:
options: 0.100 m, in 0.40 s, the most the leg may reach
questions.explanation: The swing ends 1 cm above where the ground was expected, so a 5 cm step down needs 6 cm of reaching, which at 0.25 m/s takes 0.24 s.

questions.question: What did a hole deeper than the leg may reach give?
options: A landing, 0.60 s late
A touch reported at the limit of reach, as if the ground were there
A fault, and the machine went to sit
A report of a hole after 0.40 s
questions.explanation: The search stops at 10 cm below the planned place. Having found nothing by then (0.40 s at 0.25 m/s) it reports a hole, and the leg is brought back instead of being loaded.

questions.question: Why is the ground estimate moved by a gain?
options: Because the contact sense is noisy and the gain filters the force
So that the estimate is ready before the foot lands
One stone should not lift the body, while a real change is followed
Because the feet are at different heights and the gain averages them
questions.explanation: With a gain of 0.2 one landing on a 3 cm bump moved the estimate 6.0 mm, and ten moved it 26.8 mm. A single stone hardly moves the body; ground that stays higher is followed.

questions.question: What must a swing do when the foot touches early?
options: Finish its path, so that the timing of the gait is kept
Lift again and search for the ground from the top
Stop, or the foot pushes into the bump
Speed up, so that the weight comes on sooner
questions.explanation: The foot is already on the ground. A swing that carries on drives the foot into the bump and lifts that corner of the body.

questions.question: What is not covered?
options: The limit on how far the search may reach
Looking ahead, soft ground and the slip of the foot
The body's height over ground that is not level
What happens when the foot touches before the swing ends
questions.explanation: The feet here find the ground by touch, one landing at a time. Choosing where to step needs a sensor that sees ahead, and soft or slippery ground needs more than a contact threshold.
